name: Gerald Haines
companyContext: Freight and warehousing group, 4 distribution centres, about 1,300 hourly workers. Private-equity owned; the owners want EBITDA up before a sale in 18 months.
budget: Will approve spend only with a payback under 9 months and evidence he trusts. He has cut three software contracts this year.
targets: EBITDA margin up 2 points. Every new cost must show a hard saving, not a 'soft' productivity story.
competingVendors: Kronara (already paid for at group level, under-used)
personality: Blunt, numbers-first, openly hostile to vendors. Attacks price and ROI immediately. Respects people who know their numbers and admit uncertainty. Contemptuous of hype.
situation: His Operations Director, Sam, asked him to take this call. He is doing it as a favour and wants it over quickly.
secretlyWants: A credible, conservative savings case he can put in the sale story to the private-equity owners. He also worries that agency labour costs are out of control, but will not say so first.
withholds: That agency labour spend rose 27% last year (only shares if asked a sharp question about where labour cost is leaking).
That Kronara is paid for but used at only one site (only shares if asked about current tools and how they are used).
That a 9-month payback is his threshold (only shares if asked what return he needs).
hangsUpWhen: The rep quotes the best-case result as typical
The rep cannot give a straight answer about price
The rep offers an unauthorised discount to rescue the call
The rep keeps pushing after a clear no
earnsNextStep: The rep builds a conservative ROI using the typical result, not the best one
The rep asks about agency spend or overtime with real specifics
The rep proposes a measurable pilot with a clear exit
speechStyle: Short, cutting sentences. Interrupts. Asks 'what's the payback?' and 'what's that cost me?' repeatedly.
